title: Records of Processing Activities
subtitle: Manage your Article 30 compliance records and data processing activities.
empty_state: No processing activities found. Create your first record to begin.

editor.ai_suggested_data: AI suggested {count} data categories. Apply them in the Data Categories tab.
editor.regulatory_impacts_notice: {count} regulatory update(s) may affect this activity. Review updates →

general.title: General Information
general.purpose_ph: Describe exactly why this processing occurs...
general.client_assignment_desc: Select which clients this processing activity serves. It will appear on their compliance portals.
general.systematic_monitoring_desc: Processing involves regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale.
general.status_publish_hint: An activity becomes active through Publish, once its record answers Article 30.
general.business_owner_hint: Who knows what this activity actually does day to day.
general.privacy_owner_hint: Who answers for it under Article 5(2).

legal.title: Legal Basis Configuration
legal.lia_desc: You must conduct and document an LIA when relying on legitimate interests.
legal.role_controller: Controller — we decide why and how
legal.role_joint_controller: Joint controller — we decide jointly with another
legal.role_processor: Processor — we act on another organisation’s instructions
legal.role_hint: Article 30(1) is the controller’s record; Article 30(2) is the processor’s. They require different information.
legal.controller_name_hint: Required by Article 30(2)(a) for every processor record.

retention.title: Data Retention Policy
retention.justification_ph: Explain why this data must be kept for this period (e.g., statutory requirements, business needs)...
retention.deletion_procedure_ph: How is this data securely destroyed at the end of its lifecycle?
retention.custom_ph: e.g. 7 years after the end of the employment relationship

security.title: Technical & Organizational Measures (TOMs)
security.additional_notes_ph: Describe any other specific technical or organizational measures...

editor.not_found_description: The requested processing activity could not be loaded.

completeness.title: Record completeness
completeness.complete: Every requirement that applies to this activity is answered.
completeness.complete_detail: Nothing outstanding. The record answers each Article 30 limb that applies to it.

gate.title: This record cannot be published yet
gate.description: Publishing marks an activity as an active Article 30 record. These requirements are unanswered.
gate.exception_ph: E.g. Published ahead of the September audit with the DPO's agreement; Finance is confirming the retention period.
gate.exception_hint: The reason is stored with your name and the date, and shown on the record. An override that is not written down is not an override.

adm.title: Profiling and automated decisions
adm.subtitle: Article 22. Only asked about further if this activity makes decisions without a person in the loop.
adm.profiling_desc: Article 4(4) — automated evaluation of personal aspects such as performance, preferences, behaviour or location.
adm.solely_automated: Decisions are made solely by automated means
adm.solely_automated_desc: With legal or similarly significant effects. Article 22(1) prohibits this unless 22(2)(a)-(c) applies.
adm.logic_ph: How the decision is reached, in terms a data subject could follow.
adm.logic_hint: Articles 13(2)(f) and 14(2)(g) require meaningful information about the logic — not the source code, but not "an algorithm" either.
adm.significance_ph: What the decision determines for the person it is about.
adm.human_intervention_ph: Who can review the outcome, how a subject reaches them, and what they can change.
adm.human_intervention_hint: Article 22(3) requires the right to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view and to contest the decision.

empty.title: No processing activities yet
empty.description: Your Article 30 register lists every purpose you process personal data for. Add the first activity, or import a register you already keep.
empty.filtered_description: Nothing in the register matches what you have selected. Clear the filters to see everything again.

record.subtitle: Full record — Article 30
record.name: Name
record.no_data_subjects: No categories of data subject recorded.
record.no_data_categories: No categories of personal data recorded.
record.national_law: Union or Member State law relied on
record.no_recipients: No recipients recorded. Nothing about this activity is disclosed outside the organisation.
record.no_transfers: No transfers outside the EEA recorded.
record.retention_note: Where a data category carries its own retention rule, that rule governs it. This is the fallback for anything that does not.
record.no_security: No technical or organisational measures recorded.

filters.title: Filters
filters.search_ph: Search names, purposes, categories, recipients, countries…
filters.sort_review_note: Shows only activities with a review date scheduled.

review.overdue_banner: {count, plural, one {# activity is overdue for review} other {# activities are overdue for review}}

bulk.select_page: Select every activity on this page
bulk.select_all_capped: {count} selected — the maximum for one operation
bulk.select_all_capped_hint: More activities match than one bulk operation may touch ({cap}). Narrow the filters and repeat.
bulk.no_bulk_publish: Publishing runs through the Article 30 gate one record at a time, so it is not offered here.
bulk.updated: {count, plural, one {# activity updated} other {# activities updated}}
bulk.archived: {count, plural, one {# activity archived} other {# activities archived}}
bulk.deleted: {count, plural, one {# activity deleted} other {# activities deleted}}
bulk.exported: {count, plural, one {# activity exported} other {# activities exported}}
bulk.confirm_archive_title: Archive {count, plural, one {# activity} other {# activities}}?
bulk.confirm_archive_body: Archived activities leave the register but keep everything recorded against them, and can be restored.
bulk.confirm_delete_title: Delete {count, plural, one {# activity} other {# activities}}?
bulk.confirm_delete_body: Deleting removes them from the register, its exports and its compliance score. Archiving keeps the record and is usually what is wanted.

actions.delete_body: The activity leaves the register, its exports and its compliance score. This is not the same as archiving.
actions.no_dependencies: Nothing else refers to this activity.
actions.consider_archive: Archiving keeps the record and everything recorded against it, and can be undone.

deps.clients: {count, plural, one {# client assignment} other {# client assignments}}
deps.gaps: {count, plural, one {# compliance gap} other {# compliance gaps}}
deps.assessments: {count, plural, one {# legitimate interest assessment} other {# legitimate interest assessments}}
deps.dataSubjects: {count, plural, one {# data subject category} other {# data subject categories}}
deps.dataCategories: {count, plural, one {# data category} other {# data categories}}
deps.versions: {count, plural, one {# saved version} other {# saved versions}}

review.title: Review cycle
review.subtitle: How often this record is looked at, and the signed statement that it was accurate when it was.
review.statement_ph: Accurate as at today, except that the retention period is under review.
review.statement_hint: Optional. A qualified attestation is a more honest record than a tick.

approval.title: Approval
approval.subtitle: Nothing about an Article 30 register should be editable in place by anyone, instantly.
approval.reviewer_hint: The person who wrote the record is not offered — that is the point of the workflow.
approval.you_are_reviewer: This record is waiting for your decision.
approval.reason_ph: Why this is or is not acceptable
approval.reason_hint: Required to reject. "No" without a reason is not a decision anyone can act on.

versions.title: Versions
versions.subtitle: A point-in-time copy of the whole record, kept whenever it is approved, published, or you ask.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.subtitle: Work arising from this record, assigned to someone with a date on it.
tasks.show_done: {count, plural, one {Show # closed task} other {Show # closed tasks}}
tasks.hide_done: {count, plural, one {Hide # closed task} other {Hide # closed tasks}}

comments.title: Discussion
comments.subtitle: Questions about this record, asked where the answer belongs.
comments.write_ph: Why is this retention five years?
comments.mention_hint: Type @ followed by a colleague’s name to notify them.
comments.none: Nothing has been asked about this record yet.

article_49_sub_reason.b_contract_with_subject: (b) Necessary for a contract with the subject
article_49_sub_reason.c_contract_in_subject_interest: (c) Contract concluded in the subject’s interest
article_49_sub_reason.e_legal_claims: (e) Establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims
article_49_sub_reason.f_vital_interests: (f) Vital interests, subject incapable of consent

article_9_condition.a: The subject has given explicit consent to the processing for one or more specified purposes.
article_9_condition.b: Necessary for obligations in employment, social security or social protection law. Requires Union or Member State law.
article_9_condition.c: Necessary to protect vital interests where the subject is incapable of giving consent.
article_9_condition.d: Legitimate activities of a foundation, association or not-for-profit with a political, philosophical, religious or trade-union aim.
article_9_condition.e: The data were manifestly made public by the data subject.
article_9_condition.f: Necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims, or for courts acting judicially.
article_9_condition.g: Necessary for reasons of substantial public interest. Requires Union or Member State law.
article_9_condition.h: Preventive or occupational medicine, medical diagnosis, health or social care. Requires Union or Member State law.
article_9_condition.i: Public interest in the area of public health. Requires Union or Member State law.
article_9_condition.j: Archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes. Requires Union or Member State law.

identifiability.direct: Identifies a person on its own — a name, an email address, a national ID.
identifiability.indirect: Identifies a person in combination with other data held.
identifiability.pseudonymised: Art. 4(5). Still personal data, and squarely inside the Regulation.
identifiability.anonymous: Recital 26. Outside the Regulation entirely — only if re-identification is genuinely impossible.

sensitivity.confidential: Commercially or personally sensitive without being an Art. 9 category — salary, bank details.

recipient_role.processor: Art. 28. Processes on your documented instructions and needs a DPA.
recipient_role.sub_processor: Art. 28(2). Engaged by your processor, with your prior authorisation.
recipient_role.joint_controller: Art. 26. You jointly determine purposes and means, and need an arrangement.
recipient_role.independent_controller: Determines its own purposes. The disclosure hands over controllership.

scc_year.2010: Repealed with effect from 27 December 2022. A transfer relying on these has no Art. 46 mechanism.

article_49_sub_reason.a_explicit_consent: The subject was told of the possible risks of a transfer without a mechanism, and consented anyway.
article_49_sub_reason.compelling_legitimate_interests: The 49(1) second sub-paragraph: non-repetitive, limited subjects, supervisory authority informed.

history.title: Audit Trail
history.empty: No history found for this activity.
history.no_changes: No structural changes recorded for this save.

subjects.title: Data Subject Categories
subjects.subtitle: Art. 30(1)(c) — whose personal data this activity processes. Scale feeds the Art. 35(3) DPIA screening.
subjects.child_title: Art. 8 — children’s data. Screened as high risk under Art. 35(3).
subjects.ad_hoc_title: Not from the catalogue — free text.
subjects.or_custom: Or record one not in the catalogue
subjects.custom_hint_end: to reuse it across the register.
subjects.remove_body: This removes the category from this activity. The catalogue entry itself is untouched.
subjects.empty: No data subject categories recorded. Art. 30(1)(c) requires at least one.

categories.title: Data Categories
categories.subtitle: Art. 30(1)(c) — what personal data this activity processes. Expand a row for the Art. 9(2) condition, the Art. 10 authority and the retention rule for that category.
categories.add_from_catalogue: Add from your data element catalogue...
categories.remove_body: Are you sure you want to remove this data category?
categories.retention_hint: A period without the event it runs from is not a rule — "6 years" from collection and from the end of the contract are different answers.
categories.special_condition_hint: Art. 9(1) prohibits processing this data. Recording the category without the condition that lifts the prohibition documents the problem and not the answer.
categories.national_law: Union or Member State law relied on
categories.national_law_ph: E.g. Employment Rights Act 1996 s.1; § 26 BDSG.
categories.national_law_hint: Conditions (b), (h), (i) and (j) are only available where such a law provides for them. Naming it is the difference between a condition and an assertion.
categories.criminal_hint: Art. 10 — not an Art. 9 category. It needs official authority or a specific Union or Member State authorisation of its own, which an Art. 9(2) condition does not carry.
categories.authority_ph: E.g. DBS checks under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975.
categories.source_detail_ph: Art. 14(2)(f) — where it came from, if not the subject.
categories.necessity_ph: Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation — what the purpose could not achieve without it.

recipients.select_vendor: Select a vendor from your register...
recipients.link_hint: Linking a vendor keeps DPA status in step and creates a cross-border transfer record where one is required.
recipients.other_ph: E.g. Internal HR Team, Local Auditor
recipients.remove_body: Are you sure you want to remove this data recipient?
recipients.empty: No recipients documented for this processing activity.

transfers.title: International Transfers
transfers.subtitle: Art. 30(1)(e) and Chapter V. Adequacy is computed from the Commission’s decisions; expand a row to record the mechanism itself, which is what an auditor asks to see.
transfers.adequacy_eea_title: Inside the EEA — Chapter V does not apply.
transfers.adequacy_dpf_title: Adequate for certified DPF entities only. An uncertified importer has no mechanism here.
transfers.adequacy_commercial_title: Adequacy does not reach public-sector or employee data.
transfers.adequacy_full_title: Commission adequacy decision — no Art. 46 mechanism required.
transfers.adequacy_third_title: Third country — an Art. 46 safeguard or an Art. 49 derogation is required.
transfers.remove_body: Are you sure you want to remove this data transfer?
transfers.note_inside_eea: {country} is inside the EEA, so no Art. 46 safeguard is required. Recording one does no harm, but the adequacy decision is the mechanism.
transfers.note_adequate: {country} holds an adequacy decision, so no Art. 46 safeguard is required. Recording one does no harm, but the adequacy decision is the mechanism.
transfers.note_no_mechanism: This transfer has no mechanism yet. Choose one above — a transfer to a third country without an Art. 46 safeguard or an Art. 49 derogation has no lawful route out of the EEA.
transfers.scc_repealed: Repealed with effect from 27 December 2022. This transfer has no Art. 46 mechanism until it is repapered onto the 2021 clauses.
transfers.module_hint: The module decides which party bears which obligation.
transfers.expiry_hint: The EDPB expects transfers to be re-assessed periodically.
transfers.signatories_ph: Exporting and importing entities as signed.
transfers.annexes_hint: Annex I (parties, description of the transfer) and Annex II (technical and organisational measures). Unexecuted annexes are the most common finding on an otherwise signed set of clauses.
transfers.dpf_hint: The framework covers certified organisations only, and only within the scope they certified for. Check the importer on the US Department of Commerce list before relying on it.
transfers.dpf_scope_hint: An HR transfer to an importer certified for non-HR data alone has no mechanism.
transfers.dpf_expiry_hint: Certification is renewed annually. A lapsed one takes the mechanism with it.
transfers.bcr_reference_ph: Lead supervisory authority and approval reference.
transfers.adequacy_none_hint: This destination holds no adequacy decision on the Commission list. Check the mechanism.
transfers.adequacy_commercial_hint: This decision does not reach public-sector or employee data.
transfers.adequacy_dpf_hint: US adequacy runs through the DPF and covers certified entities only — record it as DPF instead.
transfers.derogation_hint: Art. 49 is a derogation, not a safeguard. The EDPB reads it narrowly: it is for occasional, non-repetitive transfers, not for a standing data flow.
transfers.art49_justification_ph: Why the conditions of this derogation are met, and why the transfer is occasional.
transfers.mechanism_detail_ph: The approved code or certification relied on, and its scope.
transfers.tia_needed: A transfer impact assessment is required
transfers.tia_needed_hint: Schrems II. The outcome is recorded by the TIA itself and cannot be asserted here.

dpia.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment
dpia.subtitle: A DPIA is required if this processing activity is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
dpia.vendor_warning_body: Vendor {name} linked to this activity is currently flagged as {level} risk (score {score}). Consider documenting this as a residual risk.
dpia.risk_description_ph: e.g. Unauthorised access to health records via a third-party vendor
dpia.mitigation_required: Mitigation Required to Accept Residual Risk
dpia.mitigation_description_ph: e.g. Enforce MFA on all third-party endpoints and audit quarterly

catalogue.title: Register catalogues
catalogue.subtitle: The shared vocabulary your processing activities draw on. Kept here rather than typed per activity so that one element means one thing across the register — and so that "which activities process health data?" has an answer.
catalogue.archive_title: Archive — existing register entries keep the name they were recorded with.
catalogue.empty_elements: No data elements in the catalogue.
catalogue.empty_subjects: No data subject categories in the catalogue.

export_pdf_failed: Could not generate the audit report
